text:
Forensic findings CASEID
1) Domain context: A records office files intake paperwork by assigning a case identifier, date stamp, and source account. Documents are stored in the intake register with a document type, subject line, and author field. Retention is indexed by matter type; active matters stay in the working index, closed matters move to the archive with an adjudication date. Audits sample the register monthly, comparing the author field against the source account, checking date continuity, and flagging entries where the document type or subject line deviates from the matter's stated purpose. Cross-references between documents are recorded in a linking field; channels used to transmit copies are logged in the transmission field. Findings cite only these fields: register entry, document type, subject line, author, date, linking, transmission.

2) What occurred: The actor created four register entries under a single case identifier. Entry one was a document of type coordination, with a subject line referencing multiple named accounts, a linking field joining those accounts, and a date sequence indicating sequential preparation. Entry two was a document of type allocation, containing a field listing geographic subdivisions and an assignment field mapping each subdivision to one of the named accounts. Entry three was a document of type sanction, with a field listing a condition (a stated value below a group-agreed threshold) and a field listing a consequence applied to the account that met the condition. Entry four was a document of type communication, with a transmission field naming a channel not appearing elsewhere in the register, an author field, and a date later than entries one through three. The subject line of entry four referenced the absence of a detectable record.

3) Materials/access observed: The actor accessed the intake register under a named account and the archive index. The actor read register entries belonging to other named accounts (the other landlords) and the archive index of the matter. The actor wrote all four entries as author. The channel named in the transmission field of entry four was not a channel appearing in the register's standard transmission list. The geographic subdivisions in entry two matched subdivision values already present in the archive index for the matter.

4) Indicators & artifacts: Sequential date stamps across four register entries sharing one case identifier and one author account. A linking field joining multiple named accounts in a document whose subject line references joint action. An assignment field mapping geographic subdivisions to named accounts. A condition field plus consequence field in the same document, where the condition references a value threshold and the consequence references a named account. A transmission field naming a channel absent from the register's standard list. A subject line referencing the absence of a detectable record. No corresponding entries exist in the standard transmission channel log for the dates of entries one through three.
